system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update & Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note on the Seller package itself.** The "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and the [STANDARD]/[FINAL] labelling are the Seller's framing, not an agreed protocol. Nothing in our instructions records principal-level agreement on the limitation or disclosure package, and a counterparty cannot pre-clear its own clauses. Every item below has been reviewed in full regardless of label. The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence; where it matters, I note where it departs from what a buyer of a AUD 24m SaaS business would normally obtain.

---

## SPA-N-001 – General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Cap at or near 100% of price for general warranties, or at minimum 40–50%, with fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and fraud sitting outside the cap entirely (see N-004, N-005, N-011, N-016).
- **Recommendation:** Reject 20%; counter at 100%, floor fall-back 50%, with express carve-outs uncapped or capped at price.
- **Reason:** At 20% a single identified exposure (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, Riverlark AUD 3.2m) could exhaust the cap, leaving no recourse for anything else.

## SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000 per claim; basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04%); excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ≤ AUD 10,000 (with related claims aggregated); basket ≤ AUD 120,000 (0.5%); **tipping** basket (recover from dollar one once exceeded); no de minimis/basket for fundamental, tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 10k / 120k tipping; hard reject "excess only".
- **Reason:** The Sandbar renewals (3 × 110k) show how the Seller will carve exposures into pieces – aggregation of related claims and a tipping basket are essential.

## SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; limitations apply to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** General warranties 24 months (minimum covering two full audit cycles); tax 7 years (ATO amendment periods); fundamental/title 7 years or statutory limitation; specific indemnities until the underlying matter is resolved; all limitations apply **only** where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter 24 months general, 7 years tax/fundamental; delete the default-to-all-Claims language.
- **Reason:** 18 months barely covers one audited year, and the "applies to all Claims unless stated" default silently caps tax and title.

## SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency, share capital) capped at 100% of price, 7-year (or statutory) limitation, no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or buyer-knowledge qualifications.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright; this is a non-negotiable for the Buyer.
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing; recovering only AUD 4.8m is not "administrative simplicity", it is a 80% transfer of risk.

## SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None offered. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Express provision that no limitation (cap, threshold, time limit, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) applies to fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct by the Seller or its officers/agents.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out; also require non-reliance clause to exclude fraudulent misrepresentation and statutory misleading-conduct claims (ACL s18) to the extent permitted by law.
- **Reason:** Limiting liability for fraud is unenforceable in part and commercially unacceptable in whole; the Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording is an attempt to do exactly that.

## SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and *all publicly searchable records*; disclosure letter paras 1.4 and 11 deny any admission or conclusion.
- **Buyer wants:** Only matters **fairly disclosed** (with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter) in the Disclosure Letter itself count; data room disclosed only via specific cross-reference; no disclosure against fundamental, tax, or specific indemnities; public-register disclosure limited to ASIC company search, PPSR and IP Australia searches actually conducted and listed; data room contents fixed by an agreed index/USB.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general data-room and public-record disclosure; impose a "fair disclosure" standard.
- **Reason:** Combined with N-007, general disclosure of everything "discoverable" would extinguish virtually every warranty while the Seller simultaneously disclaims that any disclosure means anything (para 1.4).

## SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete clause 8.3 entirely. Fall-back only: actual (not constructive/imputed) knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals, excluding advisers, excluding anything merely "discoverable".
- **Recommendation:** Delete; the fall-back is a last resort.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable from public records" is constructive knowledge of the world – it would eliminate the warranty package and shift the Seller's duty to disclose onto the Buyer's duty to find.

## SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a **condition precedent** in the Buyer's favour: unconditional written consent (or consent with conditions the Buyer approves) satisfying cl 11.2 **and** evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met; Seller to use *best/all reasonable* endeavours; Buyer waiver right; MAC/termination if not obtained; if the Buyer elects to proceed without it, a specific indemnity (outside cap/basket) for loss of Bluefen revenue within 24 months post-Completion, or price retention/escrow of an agreed amount.
- **Recommendation:** Upgrade to CP with the above; do not accept "satisfied on delivery" of a bare letter.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of revenue; a consent subject to unmet conditions is not a consent, and the Seller's own letter admits it does not yet exist.

## SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** AUD ~3.2m facility to be released "following Completion". Disclosure para 3: not repaid, no discharge of security, change-of-control clause 8.1 engaged.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and full discharge of security (deed of release, PPSR discharges, release of any guarantees) **at or before Completion** as a Completion deliverable, funded through the funds flow from the purchase price (debt-free/cash-free adjustment); executed payout letter from Riverlark Bank as a CP; Seller indemnity for any residual amounts/break costs.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; make it a Completion deliverable funded from price.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free basis the Buyer otherwise acquires a company that still owes AUD 3.2m with a bank in a position to call default under cl 8.1 on change of control.

## SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure para 5: contingent on Completion and continued employment; no statement on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses, employer super, payroll tax and any other on-costs (estimate total ~AUD 490–510k) treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt-like items** deducted from price in the funds flow, or paid by the Seller through the Company at Completion with a specific indemnity; confirmation of who bears the cost if the continued-employment condition lapses post-Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Insert as a price deduction/debt-like item with gross-up for on-costs and specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless once the Seller owns no shares – the Company (i.e. the Buyer) will be the one writing the cheques.

## SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k) and "considered adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** (a) Pre-Completion: payment of the AUD 180k, receipt, and a **confirmatory assignment** of SOW3 Project Materials from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable (DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer conditional on payment of *every* fee); (b) specific indemnity covering loss arising from any failure of title to Ironquay-developed IP, including re-development costs, infringement claims and customer loss – outside cap/basket, 7-year period; (c) IP warranties that the Company owns all software it uses in the products.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 180k-only indemnity; require assignment at Completion plus full-loss indemnity.
- **Reason:** The exposure is not the unpaid fee but that the Company does not currently own code embedded in its SaaS product.

## SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure para 6: ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notifiability not yet established.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-signing: completed investigation report, confirmation whether the recipient accessed/deleted the file, and a documented Notifiable Data Breach assessment (Privacy Act Part IIIC; the 30-day assessment window is almost certainly already running or expired); specific indemnity for all costs, OAIC penalties, notification costs, customer claims and contract-termination losses arising from the incident – outside cap/basket, no de minimis; warranty that there are no other incidents; possible retention.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity plus completed assessment as CP; do not accept the "not material" characterisation.
- **Reason:** Business-customer data in a B2B analytics product is exactly what Bluefen-type customers will terminate over, and a late or missed OAIC notification is a Company (i.e. Buyer) liability.

## SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary course". Disclosure para 8: Seller does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of all three contracts; confirmation of whether they are one related arrangement (structured below the 25k de minimis? no – but structured so each sits under a materiality threshold); if committed and not reflected in working capital/forecast, treat as a debt-like item or price adjustment; aggregation language so related claims are treated as one; warranty that no other related supplier commitments exist.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as a single AUD 330k item; adjust price or working capital unless the Seller proves they are budgeted ordinary-course opex already in the forecast relied upon.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own letter contradicts its SPA note – it cannot be "ordinary course" in the SPA and "we don't say whether it's ordinary course" in the disclosure.

## SPA-N-014 – Category separation
- **Seller:** Single undifferentiated regime: one cap, one basket, one 18-month period applied to general, fundamental, tax, IP, specific indemnities and (implicitly) fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Explicit tiering in cl 12/13: (1) General warranties – cap/basket/24m; (2) Tax and Fundamental – 100% of price, no basket, 7 years; (3) Specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy) – uncapped or capped at price, no basket, run with the matter; (4) Fraud – no limits; and a clause that limitations apply **only** where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12–13 into the four-tier structure.
- **Reason:** Every other issue in this list is undermined if the Seller's "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default survives.

## SPA-N-015 – Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012; disclosure para 10 notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract and share-structure history, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (for any charge over the shares – note Riverlark security), inspection of share certificates, review of constitution for pre-emptive rights, confirmation no options/convertibles/ESOP; Completion deliverables of executed transfers, share certificates, and board resolutions; fundamental warranties on title unaffected by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Run the searches now (deal team action item) and require the above deliverables.
- **Reason:** A company-maintained register is the Seller's own record, not proof – and the Riverlark security may well extend to the shares.

## SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 250k basket, 18 months, general disclosure, knowledge qualifier).
- **Buyer wants:** **Tax**: a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, no basket, cap at price, 7 years, not disclosure-qualified) plus tax warranties; Seller conduct-of-claims rights limited. **IP**: full ownership/non-infringement/open-source/no-third-party-code warranties, longer period (5–7 years), higher cap, specific Ironquay carve-out (N-011); not qualified by data-room disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open; insert separate tax indemnity and IP warranty schedule.
- **Reason:** For a SaaS business the IP *is* the asset and the ATO's amendment window is 4+ years – an 18-month, 20%-capped regime covers neither.

---

## Priority ranking for the mark-up

| Tier | Issues | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Deal-critical / walk-away** | N-004, N-005, N-007, N-008, N-009, N-015 | Title, fraud, knowledge, 30% customer, AUD 3.2m debt |
| **High – price or indemnity** | N-010, N-011, N-012, N-014, N-016 | Direct cash or asset-ownership exposure |
| **Negotiable within range** | N-001, N-002, N-003, N-006, N-013 | Standard commercial limitation points |

**Aggregate identified exposure not currently protected:** Riverlark AUD 3.2m + bonuses ~AUD 0.5m + Ironquay AUD 0.18m (+ IP-title risk) + Sandbar AUD 0.33m + Bluefen revenue at risk ~AUD 3.6m p.a. + unquantified privacy liability – against a proposed AUD 4.8m cap that would also have to absorb every unknown.

**Suggested next steps:** (1) respond rejecting the [STANDARD]/[FINAL] framing and confirming all clauses are open; (2) issue DD request list for Bluefen consent/11.3 evidence, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay receipt/assignment, privacy investigation report and NDB assessment, Sandbar contracts; (3) commission ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches on the Company and the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
